newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds firm, focus on RBA after data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds firm, focus on RBA after data.

text.p: *Australian bonds finished a busier session firm after weaker then expected retail trade data was seen enhancing the chances of a further cut in domestic interest rates.
*RBA main focus after today's board meeting.
Australian bonds finished a busier session than of late, firming after weaker then expected retail trade data was seen enhancing the chances of a further cut in domestic interest rates.

The market will be closely monitoring the Reserve Bank of Australia's dealing intentions at 9.30 a.m. (2230 GMT) from Wednesday onwards following today's board meeting, and the usual time when a change in policy is announced.
However, there are mixed views as to whether the central bank will ease this month, or wait for further information on the economy and go next month.
"While the RBA could well cut rates this week, we still feel that the RBA board will wait until its March meeting before cutting rates," said economists at ANZ Securities in a report.
They saw today's data for the retail sector as supportive of a further rate cut, but felt that the central bank would want to see more information on wages and economic activity.

Average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) for the November quarter are due on Thursday, but many analysts feel that the RBA will also want to see the outcome of the national minium wage claim put forward by the trade union movement and which is due to emerge by early March.

However, today's retail trade data was undeniably weak with the monthly December report falling 1.0 percent and the fourth quarter dropping 1.3 percent. In trend terms the series is now at it lowest level in its 35 year history.

"The persistent weakness in real retail spending suggests that the combination of slower wages growth, rising unemployment and high debt levels are depressing household spending," said Louise Pollard, analyst at Nomura Research.
But Pollard also felt that the RBA would delay a rate cut so it could assess the impact of the earlier three easings, particularly the impact on business investment intentions.

Yields spreads to other dollar bloc bonds were mixed, but wiped out most of an initial widening against the U.S. and Canada following today's data. U.S. Treasuries were little changed in Tokyo from the firm levels seen in New York amid confidence that this week's FOMC will leave rates unchanged.
